[tool: bash]
I wrote the polyglot to `polyglot/main.rs`. I compiled it with both `rustc` and `g++ -x c++` and ran each binary. The two outputs matched at every N I tried: 0, 1, 2, 10, 50 and 100. For example, f(10) = 89 and f(100) = 573147844013817084101.

**How it works:**
- **Rust:** `/* /*` opens two nested block comments, because Rust nests them. The `*/` on the next line closes only one, so the whole C++ section stays commented out. The `// */` line then closes the outer comment.
- **C++:** The block comment ends at that first `*/`. The C++ code then compiles normally. `//\` ends in a backslash, which C++ treats as a line continuation, so the Rust `fn main` on the next line becomes part of a comment. Rust sees `//\` as an ordinary line comment, so it compiles that line as code.

Both versions use 128-bit unsigned integers, so values are exact up to f(185). Past that they overflow and wrap around in both languages. The C++ version uses `unsigned __int128`, which g++ supports.
